Hi Olga,

Thanks for the RACI you sent in the last call. Legal at Spark is asking for a slightly tighter definition of inspection rights in the MSA/order form. Two asks in particular:

1) Can Redwood limit inspection to a timeboxed sample window (e.g., two business days per quarter) rather than open-ended on-site review?
2) We need a concrete evidence cadence for SOC 2 control families (log retention, change control, access reviews) so our InfoSec can map to their audit schedule.

Also, do you have preferred language for pen-test coordination (advance notice, scoping, blast radius controls) that we can include as an appendix? Procurement copied here to coordinate next steps.

Thanks — can you confirm what you’d propose and whether that fits Redwood’s standard order form?

Hi Tara — thanks for outlining those points; appreciate the clarity. High-level answers below and a short proposed text block attached for the order form.

Quick answers:
- Yes, we support a timeboxed inspection approach. Our preference is a quarterly sampling window (two consecutive business days) with a remote-first posture and an on-site option if mutually agreed in advance.
- We can publish a SOC 2 evidence cadence tied to control families. See the attached sample matrix that maps control families to deliverables and typical delivery lead times (30/60/90 days).
- For pen tests: we require 10 business days advance notice, scoping plan, and an agreed blast-radius/segmentation checklist. We also prefer that third-party testers sign a short NDA and follow our test coordinator workflow.

Attached: inspection-lite-proposal.pdf (proposed MSA order-form language + sample evidence matrix) and evidence-sample-matrix.xlsx (CSV-style sheet). If you like this approach, I’ll loop legal to produce a clean redline for the order form.

Proposed next steps (suggested):
- Procurement & InfoSec confirm the quarterly window and whether Spark needs on-site or remote only.
- Redwood legal drafts the redline for the order form appendix (I’ll own).
- Agree a pen-test coordinator contact and NDA template; we’ll provide our template to speed things along.

If that works I’ll prepare the redline and a short MP (2–3 paragraphs) for the order form that limits inspection to the timeboxed cadence and preserves mutually agreed escalation for urgent investigations.

Best,
Olga

Hi Tara — thanks for the clear asks and Olga for the draft. I reviewed the inspection-lite proposal and Redwood can accept a timeboxed, sample-based inspection approach with the following legal guardrails:

- Order form appendix language: limit inspections to two consecutive business days per quarter with remote-first evidence requests; on-site visits only if both parties agree in writing at least 5 business days prior.
- Evidence cadence: attach the evidence-sample-matrix as an operational schedule; we will commit to providing the enumerated artifacts within the stated lead times (typically 30–90 days depending on the control family).
- Pen-test coordination: require 10 business days notice, NDA for testers, and a mutually agreed scope document signed by both InfoSec teams prior to execution. We also include a clause that pen tests must avoid production-impacting load (rate limits / read-only rules) and that any critical findings follow the incident disclosure timeline in the MSA.

A couple of legal notes for Spark to confirm:
1) We prefer the term ‘on-site’ to remain but are fine with ‘on-premises’ if that maps better to your policy language.
2) If Spark requires system-wide full inspections (not sample), we will need to schedule a separate inspection cadence and a written statement of business justification; otherwise the sample-based approach is standard.

If that aligns, Olga and I will produce a redline of the order form appendix and the accompanying evidence spreadsheet. I’ll send the redline tomorrow morning and include the NDA and our pen-test coordinator contact.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
